chapter_title_en: The Source of the Auditory Hallucination
chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 292: The Voice Inside Li Huowang's Head Finally Answers
chapter_meta_description: The Zuowandao impostor is about to split Li Huowang's skull when the source of his auditory hallucination finally erupts from his mouth: black tentacles, thick with blood.
og_title: He Wasn't Crazy—The Voice Was Trying to Get Out
og_description: The Zuowandao has Li Huowang pinned and gutted. Then the voice he's been shouting at for chapters answers—by ripping the impostor's face off from the inside.
twitter_title: The Answer Was Inside Him All Along
twitter_description: Li Huowang doesn't scream. He *opens his mouth*—and the Black Tai Sui answers in his place. Ch. 292.

lore_anchors.definition: A traditional northeastern Chinese spirit-summoning verse used by chuma mediums to invoke underworld officials and call upon spirit protectors.
A grotesque parasitic entity born from corrupt alchemy. It physically inhabits Li Huowang's body and has been the source of his auditory hallucinations all along.
A secret society of liars who weaponize deception as a cosmic art. Their name perverts a Daoist meditative concept into a philosophy of joyful chaos.
The rural village where Li Huowang's group has been stranded. The entire crisis was staged by a Zuowandao impostor controlling clay statues.
Title within the Zuowandao hierarchy; the impostor intends to steal this identity from Li Huowang.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What was the auditory hallucination Li Huowang kept hearing?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It was the Black Tai Sui parasitic entity living inside his body, finally confirmed when it erupted from his mouth in this chapter.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why could the Zuowandao impersonate Li Huowang so perfectly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Zuowandao use a "self-deception" technique where they fully believe their own disguise, making it undetectable even to supernatural perception.
